record.paper_title: Answering open questions in biology using spatial genomics and structured methods
record.original_question: What local spatial effects shape the clonal dynamics of dividing and differentiating cells in tissue, including how nearby cells, tissue geometry, and local niches influence clone expansion, differentiation, and dispersion?

evidence.quote: 3 What local effects shape clonal dynamics in dividing and differentiating tissue?
III. What local effects shape clonal dynamics of dividing and differentiating cells?

artifact.category_tag: spatial stochastic models of clonal dynamics
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction in spatial genomics and tissue biology. While there is an active literature on neutral drift, biased clonal competition, and lattice/Voronoi models of clonal dynamics (e.g. work by Klein, Simons, and collaborators), no single result has resolved how local neighborhoods, tissue geometry, and niches jointly shape clone size, composition, and dispersion. The problem remains an open modeling/analysis program.

status_evidence.title: Universal patterns of stem cell fate in cycling adult tissues
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews stochastic models of clonal dynamics showing neutral drift behaviors but noting open questions about spatial heterogeneity and niche effects.
status_evidence.claim: Spatial and niche effects on clonal dynamics remain incompletely characterized.

status_evidence.title: Tracing the cellular dynamics of sebaceous gland development
status_evidence.snippet: Demonstrates that tissue geometry and local niches shape clonal expansion patterns in vivo, motivating further modeling work.
status_evidence.claim: Local geometric and niche effects on clonal dynamics are an ongoing area of investigation.
